notes.text: Local password accounts introduce reusable credentials and session cookies. They must not be accepted over the current plaintext LAN listener, so controller HTTPS or an explicitly documented secure tunnel is a prerequisite for non-loopback account login.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: The earlier assessment recommended loopback by default, but the owner's existing LAN requirement remains authoritative. This record now separates a small transport improvement from deferred accounts and treats any default change as a proposal.

problem: The owner explicitly requested LAN access and the dashboard currently sends pairing credentials over HTTP. A reusable setup needs a documented secure transport option independent of any future account system.

risk.rollback: Revert the new transport configuration through an explicit operator action and preserve the existing chosen bind address. Do not silently rebind a running service or downgrade a configured secure credential path.

scope: Start with one supported secure tunnel/proxy recipe for the existing pairing-token dashboard, including API, SSE, Origin handling, and private setup instructions. Choose native controller TLS only if the actual workflow needs it.
Preserve existing LAN installation settings. A loopback default for new installations is a proposal to assess and document, not authorization to rebind or restart the owner's service.
If native TLS is selected, accept canonical local key/certificate paths, avoid storing or returning private-key contents, and apply changes through an explicit controlled restart.
Keep reusable passwords and account-mode cookies out of this slice; their secure-transport requirements remain in the account item. Do not change firewall rules or trust arbitrary proxy headers.
source: Security prerequisite identified during local-account design on 2026-08-29
title: Provide a small secure transport path for the existing LAN dashboard
validation: Verify pairing, API mutations, SSE, and expected Origin checks through the selected transport without exposing credentials in logs or documentation.
Verify invalid transport configuration fails visibly and does not silently expose a new plaintext listener.
Verify existing LAN and loopback choices remain explicit and installing documentation/configuration does not restart or rebind a running service.
value: The owner can keep LAN convenience with protected credentials, and trial users get a portable setup recipe.
